translation_notes: prefixes: BFO->bfo, ABI->abi, CCO->cco, OWL->owl, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, XSD->xsd (each with 'as NAME' to keep the Namespace object for g.bind())

Literal(x) is kept as `{Literal(x)}` wherever x can be None: `rdfs:label {Literal(self.label)}` (the entity's label is None whenever it is not set, and rdflib's Literal(None) is the plain string "None") and `{Literal(item)}` for the items of a list-valued property (a JSON null in `creator` gives the same "None" literal). A bare `{x}` raises TypeError on None in ldpy 0.7.1 (None is not an RDF term), so it would not reproduce the original, which writes the triple.

The scalar branch keeps the bare `{prop_value}`: it is only reached after `prop_value is not None`, so there Literal(prop_value) and the language's default coercion agree for str, int, float, bool, datetime and ill-typed Literal values (which is what the driver reaches). They differ for a value that is already an RDF term (URIRef/BNode become a node, not a literal); no path of the repository puts one in a data property, but `creator: Any` is not typed against it.
g += item.rdf(...) mutates in place (Graph.__iadd__ returns self), so a single @graph g at the top of the function stays valid throughout despite the later g += calls

driver.py: duck-typed Entity/Leaf fixtures (with value-based __eq__) for the property mix, an entity with no optional attribute, the cycle early return and an already-visited child; pydantic replicas of ObjectPut/ObjectDeleted filled with the values the repository gives them (label None, int 0, tz-aware and naive datetimes, creator in every JSON shape including a list holding None, an ill-typed xsd:dateTime Literal).
